Problem: Need for automatic adjustment of linear classifiers/filters without explicit matrix inversion
Result: Demonstrated rapid learning of pattern classification; foundation of adaptive filtering
Limitation: Single-layer linear; no secondary-path compensation; analog-era hardware
SilentVox relevance: Core LMS update still used in every real-time ANC engine; computational simplicity ideal for edge hardware

Paper: Widrow et al. (1975) Adaptive Noise Cancelling
Problem: Extract signal from additive noise when a correlated noise reference is available
Method: Two-input adaptive canceller (primary + reference) driven by LMS; Wiener analysis
Result: Theoretical SNR improvement = 1 / reference SNR; successful ECG, speech, antenna experiments
Limitation: Requires clean reference free of desired signal; stationary analysis dominant; no acoustic secondary path
SilentVox relevance: Canonical architecture for feed-forward noise cancellation in headsets; speech-enhancement experiments directly relevant

Paper: Morgan (1980) Multiple Correlation Cancellation Loops with Auxiliary-Path Filter
Problem: LMS convergence fails when a linear filter exists between adaptive output and error
Method: Analysis of filtered reference (filtered-x) update; general solution for secondary-path dynamics
Result: Provided convergence conditions and examples for narrowband/broadband signals
Limitation: Assumes known or fixed secondary-path model; single-channel focus
SilentVox relevance: Direct theoretical basis for FxLMS—the standard real-time acoustic ANC algorithm

Paper: Kuo & Morgan (1996) Active Noise Control Systems
Problem: Practical real-time digital ANC for broadband/narrowband/multi-channel noise
Method: Comprehensive treatment of FxLMS, feedback ANC, online secondary-path modeling, DSP implementations
Result: Became the standard engineering reference; enabled commercial DSP-based ANC products
Limitation: Pre-ML era; limited treatment of speech preservation or impulsive noise; TMS320-centric examples
SilentVox relevance: Algorithmic and DSP implementation baseline for any embedded SilentVox prototype

Problem: Traditional ANC damages speech while cancelling noise in reverberant environments
Method: End-to-end CRN with complex spectral mapping and speech-retention loss
Result: Superior noise reduction vs FxLMS on non-stationary noise; improved PESQ/STOI
Limitation: Still largely simulation or high-compute; latency and power not fully characterized for headsets
SilentVox relevance: Demonstrates feasibility of explicit speech preservation—key SilentVox differentiator

Paper: CNN-based Selective Fixed-Filter ANC (real-time multichannel window, 2024)
Problem: Continuous adaptation too slow or unstable for rapidly changing noise
Method: CNN classifies noise type and selects pre-trained fixed filters; delayless co-processor architecture
Result: Real-time multichannel cancellation with explainable LayerCAM decisions
Limitation: Requires offline training of filter bank; limited to known noise classes
SilentVox relevance: Edge-compatible selective cancellation; classification idea transferable to military noise taxonomy

Problem: Achieve sub-ms latency and low power on wearable hardware
Method: Optimized memory models, RDMA, loop-unrolled FxLMS on dual-core DSPs or Cortex-M7
Result: Sampling rates ≥38–48 kHz demonstrated; power compatible with helmet integration
Limitation: Classical algorithms still dominate; hybrid ML versions remain research prototypes
SilentVox relevance: Validates that SilentVox real-time targets are hardware-feasible today
